title: Content Upload Pipeline — Media Processing
purpose: Detailed per-file upload pipeline from Multer memory buffer through R2 upload with 3-retry exponential backoff, thumbnail generation (sharp/ffmpeg), DB insert with cleanup on failure, and fire-and-forget subscriber notification
description: The per-file content upload pipeline: Frontend sends multipart/form-data with file + metadata to POST /api/v1/content. Multer middleware parses multipart, stores file in memory buffer (1GB limit), filters by MIME type (image/* and video/* only). Content Service creates content with file processing: for each file, generate UUID filename, upload to R2 private bucket via StorageService.uploadToPrivate with 3 retries exponential backoff, then generate thumbnail (if image: sharp resize 400×400 WebP quality 80; if video: ffmpeg screenshot at 1s 400px width), upload thumbnail to R2, assemble file URLs. Insert content record in DB (status=scheduled or published based on schedule data). If DB insert fails, cleanup all uploaded files from R2. On success, fire-and-forget notifySubscribersOfNewContent. Return created content record.

securityConsiderations: 1GB memory buffer — entire file loaded in RAM before upload (OOM risk for concurrent large files)
No content moderation during upload (NSFW, copyright) — reactive only via reporting
Private R2 bucket access requires signed URLs — no public file URLs
MIME type filter prevents executable/script uploads
R2 delete on DB failure may leave orphaned files if delete fails (fixed by best-effort cleanup)
performanceConsiderations: Synchronous thumbnail generation blocks request until both upload and thumbnail complete
Only workflow with retry logic in the entire codebase (R2 upload)
Memory buffer for file storage — all file content in RAM
No CDN caching layer — signed URLs per request
Video thumbnail generation via ffmpeg is CPU-intensive
Subscriber notification is fire-and-forget but iterates all active subscribers

annotations.text: 1GB memory buffer — entire file loaded in RAM before upload via Multer memory storage. OOM risk for concurrent large file uploads.
Synchronous thumbnail generation — request blocked until both upload and thumbnail complete
Only workflow with retry logic: 3 attempts exponential backoff (500ms, 1000ms, 2000ms) for R2 upload
No CDN cache layer — signed URLs generated per-request, every page load triggers R2 API calls for files
If DB insert fails, cleanup deletes all R2 files, but if individual delete fails, orphaned files may persist
